# Prompting Vidu

Models: Vidu Q3. A good prompt runs about 1000 characters.

Name each reference where the prompt uses it as `@{ref:<ref>}`, with the exact ref you pass; Sceneform swaps in the model's own token, so wherever this guide names a token (`@Image1`, `Figure 1`), write the mention instead.

Vidu Q3 generates picture and sound together and can switch shots on its own. Vidu's smallest working prompt is subject plus action; add scene, camera, light, sound and dialogue only as the request needs them, in this order:

Scene, then subject, then action, then camera, then emotion, then sound.

**One action per shot.** Vidu names two causes of weak results: too many actions in one scene, and no camera instruction. Give the subject one physical action with at most one qualifier: "she walks forward slowly", "he turns to face the camera".

**Camera.** Lead with the shot size or angle, then add the move as its own phrase at the end of the shot: "Low angle, a cyclist crests the hill. Slow push-in." Vidu's terms: wide establishing shot, long shot, full-body framing, close-up, extreme close-up, low angle, high angle, bird's eye view, overhead shot, over-the-shoulder shot, slow pan, follow from behind, push-in, tilt, zoom. One angle per shot. Give every move a direction and a speed ("slow pan right"), and let either the camera or the subject drive the shot; when both move, tie them together ("she runs toward camera, slow pan right to follow"). A subject walking right while the camera tilts left comes out as jitter.

**Several shots.** Only when the request carries distinct beats, number them ("Shot 1: ... Shot 2: ...") and give each shot its own framing, its action, and its own line of dialogue or sound. For a two-person conversation, frame one speaker over the other's shoulder.

**Sound.** Q3 renders dialogue, effects, ambience and music in one pass. Describe each layer the scene needs: the room or weather, the sounds the action makes, and any music. Put spoken lines in quotation marks after the speaker, with a word for the voice: a woman says brightly, "We made it." When the scene should have no music or no speech, say so plainly in the sound sentence.

**Text in the frame.** Q3 draws text as part of the picture. Quote the exact words.

**With a start frame.** The image is the anchor, and the prompt says what happens next: the direction and size of the motion and what the camera does, as in Vidu's own example, "The astronaut waved and the camera moved up." With a start and an end frame, describe the motion that connects them.

**References.** Up to four reference images keep a person, product or place consistent. Say in words what each one supplies ("the woman from the first reference image", "the kitchen from the second"), then write the action, camera and sound without describing the referenced subject's appearance again.

**Avoid.** Prompts with no concrete subject or setting. Several actions inside one shot. Stacked angles or stacked moves in one shot. Conflicting directions between subject and camera.
